summary: Full author-manuscript extraction of negligible abelian-kernel embedding classes and odd-prime nonliftable representations over a p-variable rational field. Reuse pinned low-degree cohomology and upstream planned Kummer/five-term/Mackey theory; propose separate cohomological and explicit inverse-Galois continuations. Checkpoint status retains the false unrestricted Lemma 4.1, unproved Remark 5.8(2), inaccessible final-version comparison and prerequisite-source closure for follow-up. No claim of formalization. Continuation codex-a71f92 closes Remark 5.8(2) by an explicit two-carry cocycle decomposition and an independent Kummer-character lift, and routes the Lemma 4.1 counterexample as a negative acceptance theorem. Every missing item has one owner. Partial status remains for source/version and prerequisite closure, not for the N-restriction claim.

items.name: Absolute Galois group
items.statement: For any field K, Γ_K is Aut_K(K^sep) with the Krull topology. It is profinite; compare with the algebraic-closure carrier through restriction.
items.note: API: Reuse the carrier, restriction and topology instances, and finite-quotient maps; never replace the separable closure by the full closure when taking field invariants. Tests: A separably closed field has trivial Γ; retain an imperfect field as a carrier-comparison test.

items.name: Continuous second cohomology
items.statement: For a topological group Γ and a discrete abelian Γ-module A with continuous action, H²(Γ,A)=Z²_cont/B²_cont, where the coboundaries use continuous 1-cochains. For finite H give H the discrete topology.
items.note: API: Reuse Z2, B2, H2pi and representative equality; provide paper notation adapters on the existing carrier. Tests: Zero cocycle; a continuous coboundary is zero; a finite group agrees with the discrete group model after the existing/planned comparison.

items.name: Weak solution of an abelian-kernel embedding problem
items.statement: Given finite groups 1→A→G→H→1, A abelian with the conjugation H-action, K a field and continuous ρ:Γ_K→H, a weak solution is a continuous homomorphism ρ̃:Γ_K→G whose composite is ρ. No surjectivity is imposed.
items.note: API: Construct from a commuting lift; project to ρ̃; extensionality by the underlying homomorphism; pull back in K and in the extension. Tests: Split extension; trivial ρ; a lift with proper image is still weak, not a proper solution.

items.name: Universal solvability over a base field
items.statement: An abelian-kernel extension has a positive embedding-problem answer over F if every continuous Γ_K→H lifts for every field extension K/F.
items.note: API: Introduction/elimination with both quantifiers; invariance under extension equivalence; monotonicity under extending F. Tests: A split extension has the property; checking K=F alone is not the definition.

items.name: Negligible cohomology
items.statement: For finite H, an H-module A and d≥0, H^d_neg,F(H,A) is the subgroup of classes α such that ρ*α=0 for every extension K/F and continuous ρ:Γ_K→H, using A with its pulled-back discrete action.
items.note: API: Membership iff all evaluations vanish; subgroup operations, coefficient and group functoriality, base-extension monotonicity; distinguish the ambient H² from the generated subgroup used later. Tests: The zero class is negligible; a split extension gives a negligible degree-two class; do not assume nontrivial classes vanish merely over F.

items.name: Factor sets classify degree-two classes
items.statement: For a group H and abelian multiplicative H-module A, normalized factor sets modulo cohomology are in bijection with H²(H,A).
items.note: Read the pinned source GroupTheory/GroupExtension/Cohomology.lean:226. This is the abstract factor-set statement, not yet the continuous lifting criterion.

items.name: A factor-set extension splits iff its class is zero
items.statement: The extension associated to a factor set α admits a homomorphic section exactly when its H² class vanishes.
items.note: Pinned source line 245. Continuity and the pullback extension still need the next item.

items.name: Continuous obstruction criterion
items.statement: For finite H, finite H-module A, an extension class α and continuous ρ:Γ_K→H, a continuous lift exists iff ρ*α=0 in H²_cont(Γ_K,A). Thus negligibility is equivalent to universal weak solvability.
items.note: Use continuous factor sets: a continuous primitive produces a continuous lift; an abstract splitting alone does not establish this result.

items.name: Galois H-algebra
items.statement: For finite H and field K, a Galois H-algebra is a finite étale K-algebra M with H-action, M^H=K and dim_K M=|H| (equivalently an H-torsor). It need not be a field.
items.note: API: Carrier, H-action, invariants and rank; base change, algebra isomorphisms and restriction/quotient of torsors. Tests: The split algebra K^H is allowed; a field torsor is the connected case.

items.name: Galois algebras and continuous homomorphisms
items.statement: Isomorphism classes of Galois H-algebras over K correspond to Hom_cont(Γ_K,H)/H-conjugacy. For 1→A→G→H→1, a lift of ρ corresponds to a G-Galois algebra whose A-invariant algebra is the H-algebra of ρ.
items.locator: §1.2; KMRT98 Example 28.15 as used in Lemma 3.2
items.note: Import finite étale Galois-category equivalence from IG.0; prove the equivariant torsor refinement and the compatibility with taking A-invariants.

items.name: Generic Galois extension
items.statement: A faithful finite-dimensional representation V of finite H over F makes L=F(V) a Galois extension of K=F(V)^H with group H, inducing a surjective continuous Γ_K→H after an embedding L⊂K^sep.
items.note: API: Fixed-field inclusion, quotient map of Γ, faithful-action/Galois proof, base-field extension and change of separable-closure embedding. Tests: The regular representation works over every field; H=1 gives L=K; V must be faithful.

items.name: Generic criterion for negligibility
items.statement: For finite H, any H-module A, α∈H²(H,A), any field F and faithful finite-dimensional F-representation V, α is negligible over F iff its inflation in H²(F(V)^H,A) is zero. Equivalently every embedding problem for α has a weak solution iff this generic one does.
items.locator: Proposition 2.1 p.5; GM22 Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 pp.2–3
items.note: GM22 directly read. The generic criterion is also valid in every degree; its proof uses the next four inputs, not Hilbert irreducibility.

items.name: Cohomological injectivity under adjoining a variable
items.statement: For a field K, discrete Γ_K-module A and d≥0, restriction H^d(K,A)→H^d(K(t),A) is injective.
items.locator: GM22 Proposition 2.1 proof p.3, used by Proposition 2.1
items.note: Required to pass from finite K to infinite K in the versality argument; a rational place/specialization or a section after passing to K((t)) supplies the retraction. Formalize the coefficient inflation and the chosen separable closures.

items.name: Free open subset of a faithful representation
items.statement: For faithful finite H-action on a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, there is a nonempty invariant open U⊂V with free action, and U→U/H is a finite étale H-torsor; such opens give the generic field Spec F(V)^H as their limit.
items.note: This is a quotient with trivial stabilizers; characteristic dividing |H| does not obstruct étaleness of a constant finite group torsor.

items.name: Versality over infinite fields
items.statement: For infinite K/F and any H-torsor N/K, every nonempty free invariant open U in a faithful F-representation has a K-point of U/H whose pullback torsor is N.
items.locator: GM22 Proposition 2.1 proof p.3, citing GMS03 I §5
items.note: Use the twist of the vector space by N, a K-vector space with a nonempty open; this supplies the needed point. This is a weak versality theorem, not a generic-polynomial theorem.

items.name: Étale limit and edge-map compatibility in the generic criterion
items.statement: For the free invariant opens U, an H-cohomology class vanishing in H^d(F(V)^H,A) vanishes in H^d_et(U/H,A) for some U; pulling it back at a K-point yields precisely its Γ_K evaluation on the corresponding torsor.
items.note: Track the locally constant sheaf determined by A and the Hochschild–Serre edge map; require étale cohomology continuity for this affine inverse-limit system.

items.name: Trivial-action H¹ is continuous Hom
items.statement: For a trivial continuous action on A, H¹_cont(Γ,A) is canonically the additive group of continuous homomorphisms Γ→A.
items.note: Actual statement read at LowDegree.lean:840. Apply to Γ_L after pulling back the H-module along Γ_L→1.

items.name: Kummer isomorphism
items.statement: For n≥1 invertible in a field K, K×/(K×)^n≅H¹(K,μ_n), with its natural Γ_K-action. If μ_n⊂K the cocycles are continuous characters.
items.note: The pin has the class map and injectivity, not surjectivity or the isomorphism. Do not mark the full result built.

items.name: Kummer cocycle map
items.statement: For n invertible in K, a∈K× and α∈(K^sep)× with α^n=a, send a to the class of σ↦σ(α)/α in H¹(K,μ_n); its class is independent of α.
items.note: API: Reuse multiplicativity, root independence, ker_kummerMap and the quotient map; attach coefficient-action comparisons explicitly. Tests: An nth power has trivial class; n=1; a changed nth root has the same cohomology class.

items.name: Profinite Hilbert 90
items.statement: For a Galois extension L/K with profinite Galois group acting on discrete L×, H¹(Gal(L/K),L×)=0; in particular H¹(K,(K^sep)×)=0.
items.note: Read NSW proof and pinned audit: finite-level Hilbert 90 is available, but the profinite assembly is planned upstream.

items.name: Cyclic degree-two cohomology
items.statement: For finite cyclic H=<σ> and any H-module A, H²(H,A)≅A^H/N_H A.
items.note: Read FiniteCyclic.lean:80 with i=2: the declared target is the homology of A --norm--> A --(σ−1)--> A, i.e. the displayed quotient. Its cup-periodicity refinement is separate from this carrier calculation.

items.name: All cyclic central classes negligible with enough roots
items.statement: For m,n≥1 and F containing a primitive mn-th root, every class in H²(C_m,Z/n) with trivial action is negligible over F. The extension C_mn→C_m gives a generator; for every K/F the Kummer quotient map K×/(K×)^mn→K×/(K×)^m is surjective.
items.note: Correct the draft’s F×/Γ_F in the proof to K×/Γ_K, since the negligibility assertion quantifies over K/F.

items.name: Negligibility and coefficient maps
items.statement: An H-module homomorphism B→A maps H²_neg,F(H,B) into H²_neg,F(H,A).

items.name: Negligibility and group pullback
items.statement: For finite H′→H and H-module A, pullback maps H²_neg,F(H,A) into H²_neg,F(H′,A).

items.name: Negligibility and corestriction
items.statement: For H′≤H finite and any H-module A, cor maps H²_neg,F(H′,A) into H²_neg,F(H,A).
items.note: Use the generic criterion with F(V)^H′/F(V)^H and the inflation/corestriction square.

items.name: Prime-to-exponent detection
items.statement: For finite H, finite H-module A and H′≤H with gcd([H:H′],e(A))=1, α is negligible over F iff res α is negligible over F.
items.note: Reverse implication uses cor res=[H:H′] and multiplication by the index invertible on H²(H,A), not merely injectivity of res on ambient cohomology.

items.name: Negligibility under base extension
items.statement: If L/F is any field extension, H²_neg,F(H,A)⊂H²_neg,L(H,A).

items.name: Degree-two inflation
items.statement: For topological Γ, normal subgroup N and coefficient module A, inflation sends H²(Γ/N,A^N) to H²(Γ,A) by pullback and inclusion of invariants.
items.note: API: Reuse representative formula and equality to compatible-pair pullback; distinguish inflation from restriction. Tests: N=1; inflation followed by restriction to N is zero in positive degree.

items.name: Degree-two corestriction
items.statement: For an open finite-index U≤Γ and continuous topological Γ-module A, cor:H²(U,A)→H²(Γ,A) is the transversal-sum map on cocycles, independent of the chosen transversal.
items.note: API: Reuse additivity, cocycle formula and coefficient naturality; supply openness and finite index. Tests: U=Γ; two transversals produce equal classes, not necessarily identical cochains.

items.name: Corestriction after restriction
items.statement: For open finite-index U≤Γ and x∈H²(Γ,A), cor(res(x))=[Γ:U]x.

items.name: Degree-(0,2) and (2,0) projection formulas
items.statement: For an equivariant continuous bilinear pairing M×N→P and open finite-index U≤Γ, cor(res(a)∪b)=a∪cor(b) for a∈H⁰(Γ,M),b∈H²(U,N), and cor(b∪res(a))=cor(b)∪a in the reversed degrees.
items.note: Both statements read at ProjectionFormula.lean:202,221; nontrivial coefficient actions are supported.

items.name: Inflation/corestriction compatibility
items.statement: For profinite Γ, closed normal N and open U containing N, inf_Γ/N^Γ cor_U/N^Γ/N = cor_U^Γ inf_U/N^U on cohomology of a Γ/N-module.
items.note: Read NSW statement. This compatible-quotient descent identity is requested of R02.2; existing cor res alone does not supply it.

items.name: Continuous Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: For profinite Γ, closed normal N and discrete Γ-module A, E₂^{i,j}=H^i(Γ/N,H^j(N,A)) converges to H^{i+j}(Γ,A); use its edge maps with their specified signs.

items.name: Transgression and five-term exactness
items.statement: For profinite Γ and closed normal N, tg:H¹(N,A)^{Γ/N}→H²(Γ/N,A^N), with Im(tg)=Ker(inf to H²(Γ,A)). In L/K finite H-Galois and A an H-module, this is H¹(L,A)^H→H²(H,A)→H²(K,A).
items.note: Draft (2.3) wrongly prints H²(L,A) and calls the displayed segment short exact. The terminal term is H²(K,A), and only exactness at the middle is asserted here. API: Use the upstream continuous lift-and-differentiate construction, its section-independence and both adjacent maps. Tests: Split group extension has zero tg; the target of inflation is cohomology of Γ_K, not Γ_L.

items.name: Negligible subgroup as transgression image
items.statement: For faithful H-representation V/F and any H-module A, H²_neg,F(H,A)=Im[H¹(F(V),A)^H→H²(H,A)].

items.name: Transgression equals negative extension evaluation
items.statement: For profinite Γ and open normal N acting trivially on discrete A, put Δ=N/closure([N,N]) and let u be the class of 1→Δ→Γ/closure([N,N])→Γ/N→1. Then tg(x)=−u∪x, pairing Δ with Hom_cont(Δ,A).
items.locator: Lemma 2.5 proof p.7; Proposition 3.1 proof p.10; NSW (2.4.4) pp.114–117
items.note: NSW source and proof read. Since Γ/N is finite its cochains into Δ are automatically continuous; retain continuous Hom in the evaluation pairing. This is an edge-map normalization in the existing Hochschild–Serre owner.

items.name: Transgression/corestriction square
items.statement: For finite H-Galois L/K, H′≤H and H-module A, tg_H(N_H/H′ x)=cor_H′^H(tg_H′ x), where x∈H¹(L,A)^H′.
items.note: Correct the proof’s reversed u/u′: −cor(res(u)∪x)=−u∪N(x). The square itself is correctly typed.

items.name: Inverse Tate twist with finite coefficients
items.statement: Given n≥1, nA=0 and a field containing μ_n, define A(−1)=Hom_Z(μ_n,A), with H acting through A and trivially on μ_n.
items.note: API: Evaluation, coefficient maps, H-action, extensionality and comparison under replacing n by a multiple. Tests: A=μ_n gives Z/n; A=0; equivariance of evaluation requires the stated trivial action on μ_n.

items.name: Evaluation identification
items.statement: Under nA=0 and μ_n cyclic of order n, evaluation A(−1)⊗_Z μ_n→A is an H-module isomorphism; it restricts to A(−1)^H⊗μ_n≅A^H.
items.note: Identify μ_n with Z/n using a primitive root to prove bijectivity, but the evaluation map itself is canonical.

items.name: Tensor–Kummer isomorphism ι
items.statement: For finite H-module A killed by n, H-Galois L/K, and μ_n⊂K, ι:A(−1)⊗_Z L×≅H¹(L,A), obtained from Kummer and the cup/evaluation pairing, is H-equivariant.
items.note: API: Value on a⊗f is the pushforward by a:μ_n→A of the Kummer class of f; coefficient naturality, H-equivariance and field restriction/norm compatibility. Tests: A=μ_n recovers Kummer; finite direct sums; n may exceed e(A).

items.name: Tensor–Kummer isomorphism proof by cyclic summands
items.statement: With the preceding hypotheses, cup H⁰(L,A(−1))⊗H¹(L,μ_n)→H¹(L,A) is bijective: decompose the finite abelian group A into cyclic summands and use Kummer reduction maps for orders dividing n.
items.note: The Γ_L-action is trivial, but the external H-action on A need not be trivial. Prove H-equivariance by naturality after proving the underlying isomorphism; do not assert the cyclic decomposition is H-equivariant.

items.name: The gamma map
items.statement: For finite H-module A killed by n and H-Galois L/K with μ_ne⊂K, e(H)|e, define γ:(A(−1)⊗L×)^H→H²(H,A) as tg∘ι.
items.note: API: Additivity, coefficient and field functoriality, restriction of H and compatibility with subgroup norms after Lemma 2.5. Tests: H=1 gives zero; A=μ_n gives transgression of Kummer classes; constants vanish in the generic situation only after the separate proof.

items.name: Two connecting homomorphisms
items.statement: With e,n,H,L/K as in §3, ∂₁:(L×/μ_e)^H→H¹(H,μ_e) comes from 1→μ_e→L×→L×/μ_e→1, and ∂₂:H¹(H,μ_e)→H²(H,μ_n) from 1→μ_n→μ_ne→μ_e→1, the last map being nth power.
items.note: API: Explicit cocycles ∂₁(fμ_e)(h)=h(f)/f, naturality, exactness and ∂₂ as the pullback extension class. Tests: An invariant unit in K× has zero ∂₁; e=1; do not apply a trivial-action lemma to the first sequence’s L× term.

items.name: Invariant cosets yield invariant tensor classes
items.statement: If fμ_e is H-invariant, nA=0 and μ_ne⊂K, then a⊗f is H-invariant for a∈A(−1)^H. Indeed h(f)/f∈μ_e⊂(L×)^n, which dies after tensoring with A(−1).

items.name: The beta map
items.statement: Under §3 hypotheses, β:A(−1)^H⊗(L×/μ_e)^H→(A(−1)⊗L×)^H sends a⊗fμ_e to a⊗f; it is independent of representatives because μ_e consists of nth powers in L×.
items.note: API: Bilinearity, evaluation on pure tensors, coefficient naturality and invariance/representative-independence lemmas. Tests: Changing f by an eth root does not change β; an invariant coset is required, not an arbitrary unit.

items.name: Kummer character extends through μ_ne
items.statement: For e(H)|e, H-Galois L/K, μ_ne⊂K and fμ_e∈(L×/μ_e)^H, the Kummer character ρ_f:Γ_L→μ_n extends to a character Γ_K→μ_ne fitting over ∂₁(fμ_e):H→μ_e and the nth-power quotient.
items.note: The character need not be surjective. Use the Galois algebra construction below or an nth root r of f and σ↦σ(r)/r; its nth power is in μ_e and all μ_ne are fixed by Γ_K.

items.name: The finite étale algebra and its extension group
items.statement: For the same f, M=L[t]/(t^n−f) is finite étale over L. Choose c_h∈μ_ne with c_h^n=h(f)/f, extend h by t↦c_h t, and let G be all ζh̃. Then 1→μ_n→G→H→1 is central and M/K is a G-Galois algebra.
items.note: API: Action on L and t; multiplication up to a μ_n cocycle; independence up to isomorphism of the c_h choices; fixed algebra and rank. Tests: f an nth power gives a disconnected algebra; do not treat M automatically as a field; n invertible is required for étaleness.

items.name: The character of the Kummer algebra
items.statement: For the above G-action on M, χ(g)=g(t)/t lies in μ_ne and is a homomorphism restricting to id on μ_n; χ(g)^n=∂₁(fμ_e)(g mod μ_n).
items.note: API: Evaluation, restriction, quotient square and independence from the chosen root up to the torsor identification. Tests: A scalar ζ acts by χ(ζ)=ζ; t is a unit since f≠0.

items.name: Anticommutativity of the gamma–beta diagram
items.statement: For e(H)|e, nA=0, μ_ne⊂K and H-Galois L/K, γβ(a⊗fμ_e)=−a∪∂₂∂₁(fμ_e).
items.note: Keep the minus sign. Reduce by coefficient naturality to A=μ_n, use the preceding character diagram and tg(id)=−[μ_ne].

items.name: Cup–corestriction generators
items.statement: For H′≤H define φ_H′:A^H′⊗H²(H′,Z)→H²(H,A), a⊗c↦cor_H′^H(a∪c).
items.note: API: Additivity in both entries, projection formula, conjugation covariance and transitivity under subgroup enlargement. Tests: H′=H is cup product; H′=1 contributes zero in degree two; the Z action is trivial.

items.name: The generated subgroup
items.statement: Write barH²(H,A) for the subgroup of H²(H,A) generated by the images of all φ_H′, H′≤H; this is not the whole ambient cohomology by definition.
items.note: API: Generator membership, subgroup induction, monotonicity in collections of subgroups, compatibility with coefficients and conjugation. Tests: H=1 and A=0; use a distinct identifier because PDF text extraction loses the source overbar.

items.name: Cohomological universal coefficient exact sequence
items.statement: For finite H, trivial H-module X and i≥0, there is a natural exact sequence 0→H^i(H,Z)⊗X→H^i(H,X)→Tor₁^Z(H^{i+1}(H,Z),X)→0. The first map is cup product; no canonical splitting is asserted.
items.note: Finite H is essential to commute the finite-rank bar cochains with arbitrary direct sums. Construct using a length-one free Z-resolution of X, the long exact sequence and the displayed kernel/cokernel identifications; this is additional finite-coefficient API beyond upstream’s listed targets.

items.name: Tor monomorphism for an injection of abelian groups
items.statement: For any abelian group C and injection X→Y, Tor₁^Z(C,X)→Tor₁^Z(C,Y) is injective, because Tor₂^Z=0.
items.note: Need only this exactness consequence, not the stronger and false assertion that Tor₁ is an exact functor. Import general Tor/projective resolutions; prove the Z-specialized statement once.

items.name: Connecting classes lie in the integral cup image
items.statement: For finite H and exact 0→X→Y→Z₀→0 of abelian groups all with trivial H-action, Im[H¹(H,Z₀)→H²(H,X)]⊂Im[H²(H,Z)⊗X→H²(H,X)].
items.note: Z₀ here is the variable third module; Z in H²(H,Z) is the integers. Follow the natural UCT diagram and Tor monomorphism, not a nonexistent canonical splitting.

items.name: Normed gamma classes belong to a single generator image
items.statement: For e(H)|e, nA=0, μ_ne⊂K, H-Galois L/K, H′≤H, a∈A(−1)^H′ and fμ_e∈(L×/μ_e)^H′, γ_H(N_H/H′(a⊗f))∈Im φ_H′.
items.note: Apply Lemma 3.4 to (3.3), not (3.2) as the draft prints. The μ_n→μ_ne→μ_e sequence has trivial actions. Combine Proposition 3.1, evaluation and norm/tg compatibility.

items.name: Independence of the chosen annihilator
items.statement: If e(A)|n and the relevant roots exist, the canonical power quotient π:μ_n→μ_e(A) induces π*:Hom(μ_e(A),A)≅Hom(μ_n,A), and under this isomorphism both ι and γ agree for the two annihilators.
items.note: Split into separate twist, ι and γ compatibility nodes in the blueprint. Here they are one simultaneous naturality assertion as in the source.

items.name: Generic gamma image is the negligible subgroup
items.statement: Under finite H,A and μ_e(A)e(H)⊂F, for faithful V/F one has H²_neg,F(H,A)=Im[(A(−1)⊗F(V)×)^H --γ--> H²(H,A)].

items.name: Divisors of affine representation space
items.statement: For V an affine space over F, Div(V) is the free abelian group on codimension-one points, with its induced H-action when H acts linearly on V.
items.note: API: Finite-support sums, valuation coefficients, H-action and orbit/stabilizer decomposition; principal divisor map from F(V)×. Tests: For A¹, irreducible polynomials give prime divisors; the divisor of a nonzero constant is zero.

items.name: Divisor exact sequence for affine space
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional vector space V/F, 1→F×→F(V)× --div--> Div(V)→0 is exact, and each codimension-one prime has a generator f_x unique up to F×.
items.note: Use factoriality of the polynomial coordinate ring and its units; this is arbitrary-dimensional affine space, not the projective-curve divisor theory of SF.3.

items.name: Tensoring the divisor sequence preserves exactness
items.statement: For any abelian group B, tensoring (4.2) over Z gives 0→B⊗F×→B⊗F(V)×→B⊗Div(V)→0, since the final term before tensoring is free abelian.

items.name: Invariants of a permutation module with diagonal coefficients
items.statement: For finite H acting on a set S and H-module B, (B⊗Z[S])^H is the direct sum over H-orbits of copies of B^H_s, identified by b↦Σ_{h∈H/H_s}h(b)⊗h(s).
items.note: Finite H ensures each orbit is finite. The statement is about the divisor module, not arbitrary chosen unit lifts.

items.name: Divisor-stabilizer character
items.statement: If H acts F-linearly on V, x is a prime divisor fixed by H_x and div(f_x)=x, then h↦h(f_x)/f_x is a homomorphism H_x→F×. Its image lies in μ_e for any e divisible by e(H).

items.name: Corrected invariant-generator lemma under roots hypotheses
items.statement: Let H finite, B killed by n≥1, V a faithful F-representation, e(H)|e and μ_ne⊂F. Then (B⊗F(V)×)^H is generated by (B⊗F×)^H and N_H/H_x(b⊗f_x), for x prime divisors and b∈B^H_x.
items.locator: Lemma 4.1 as used in Theorem 1.3, pp.12–14
items.note: Repair the printed lemma by the hypotheses actually available in the application. The stabilizer character takes values in μ_e⊂(F×)^n, so b⊗f_x is H_x-invariant; the orbit generators therefore lift to invariants, proving the needed surjectivity after invariants. Exactness alone does not prove this.

items.name: Printed Lemma 4.1 without roots hypotheses fails
items.statement: The printed assertion for arbitrary F and finite H-module B cannot be used as stated: take H=C₂ acting on V=A¹_R by t↦−t, B=Z/2 with trivial action, x=(t), and f_x=t. H_x=H, but the claimed generator 1⊗t in R(t)×/(R(t)×)² is not fixed, since its translate differs by the nontrivial class of −1.
items.note: Route as a true negative acceptance theorem, not the false unrestricted lemma. If −1=(f/g)² in R(t), then f²+g²=0 with g nonzero, impossible by the positive leading coefficient of a nonzero sum of real polynomial squares. Thus the proposed generator is non-invariant. The counterexample and corrected /63 are settled at manuscript level; comparing final JAMS wording is a separate provenance task.

items.name: Finite tensor divisible group vanishes
items.statement: If B is finite and D is a divisible abelian group, then B⊗_Z D=0: choose n killing B and write every d as n d′.

items.name: Gamma kills constants in the generic extension
items.statement: For finite H,A with the classification roots hypotheses, the generic γ vanishes on (A(−1)⊗F×)^H.
items.note: Base change to an algebraic closure makes its unit group divisible. Naturality leaves the target H²(H,A) unchanged; it is not necessary for (A(−1)⊗F×)^H itself to vanish over F.

items.name: Integral second cohomology as characters
items.statement: For finite H with trivial action on Z, the connecting map H¹(H,Q/Z)→H²(H,Z) is an isomorphism; hence H²(H,Z)≅Hom(H,Q/Z).
items.locator: Theorem 1.3 proof p.13; Claim 5.5; NSW p.52
items.note: Use H^i(H,Q)=0 for i>0. Each character has finite cyclic image of exponent dividing e(H).

items.name: Vanishing with rational coefficients
items.statement: For finite H and a rational H-module W, H^i(H,W)=0 for i>0.
items.note: The upstream all-degree annihilation/torsion scope includes rational vanishing. The pin’s degree-two cor/res identity is not an all-degree proof.

items.name: Cup generators are negligible
items.statement: For finite H,A and F containing μ_e(A)e(H), every a∈A^H and c∈H²(H,Z) has a∪c negligible. Therefore barH²(H,A)⊂H²_neg,F(H,A).
items.note: Factor the character for c through a cyclic group C_m with m|e(H), use the map Z/e(A)→A sending 1 to a, and apply cyclic negligibility, pullback, pushforward and corestriction.

items.name: Negligible classes are generated by cup–corestrictions
items.statement: For finite H,A and F containing a primitive e(A)e(H)-th root, H²_neg,F(H,A)=barH²(H,A), generated by cor_H′^H(a∪c) for all H′≤H, a∈A^H′ and c∈H²(H′,Z).
items.note: The reverse inclusion uses generic γ, constants killed after algebraic-closure base change, the corrected invariant-generator lemma and Proposition 3.3. Keep the product e(A)e(H), not lcm or either exponent alone.

items.name: Independence of the base field with enough roots
items.statement: For fixed finite H,A, all fields containing μ_e(A)e(H) have the same negligible subgroup of the fixed abstract H²(H,A), namely barH²(H,A).

items.name: Stabilizer-only generators
items.statement: With Theorem 1.3 hypotheses and H_a={h∈H:h(a)=a}, the negligible subgroup is generated by cor_H_a^H(a∪χ), a∈A, χ∈H²(H_a,Z).
items.note: The source says centralizer of a in H; for a general H-module this is the action stabilizer. Use H′≤H_a, transitivity and the projection formula.

items.name: Kummer extension class
items.statement: For m,n≥1 with μ_mn⊂F, a Kummer class is the central extension class of 0→Z/n→Z/mn→Z/m→0, with the last map reduction and the first multiplication by m.
items.note: API: Explicit inclusion/quotient maps, action triviality, exactness and its H² representative; comparison under cyclic identifications. Tests: m=1 or n=1; specify the kernel identification, not merely the middle group.

items.name: Generation from Kummer classes
items.statement: Classes obtained by finitely many coefficient pushforwards, group pullbacks and subgroup corestrictions from Kummer classes are negligible. If F contains μ_e(A)e(H), their images in H²(H,A) generate all negligible classes.
items.note: Only those starting Kummer classes whose mn-th roots lie in F are allowed. The set of obtained classes is stated to be a generating set, not assumed closed under sums by definition.

items.name: General-linear reduction extension
items.statement: For prime p and n≥1, reduction gives 0→M_n(F_p)→GL_n(Z/p²)→GL_n(F_p)→1, with kernel map X↦I+pX and action g·X=gXg⁻¹.
items.note: API: Reduction, lift of an invertible matrix, kernel identification, additive product law and conjugation formula; cohomology class functorial under block inclusions. Tests: (I+pX)(I+pY)=I+p(X+Y); a lift of a determinant nonzero modulo p is invertible; n=1.

items.name: Upper-triangular reduction extension
items.statement: For prime p and n≥1, reduction gives 0→b_n(F_p)→B_n(Z/p²)→B_n(F_p)→1, where b_n is the additive group of upper-triangular matrices with the conjugation action.
items.note: API: Use the same reduction/kernel construction restricted to upper-triangular matrices; compare to the GL extension by inclusion of groups and coefficients. Tests: Every diagonal entry remains a unit on lifting; kernel matrices must be upper triangular; the comparison square is a pushout after restriction.

items.name: A modulo-p² lift
items.statement: For a field K and continuous ρ:Γ_K→GL_n(F_p), a modulo-p² lift is continuous ρ̃:Γ_K→GL_n(Z/p²) reducing to ρ; the analogous B_n lift keeps the full ordered flag.
items.note: API: Lift predicate, reduction equation, field restriction, conjugation and direct sum with trivial representations. Tests: An abstract lift of the matrix image group is sufficient but not necessary; preserve continuity and the specified residual representation.

items.name: One-dimensional lifting
items.statement: For every prime p the reduction (Z/p²)×→F_p× splits, so every one-dimensional residual Galois representation over any field lifts modulo p².
items.note: Include as boundary-case acceptance, with p=2 treated directly; this does not imply a splitting for higher ranks.

items.name: Prime-to-p index of the Borel and Sylow subgroup
items.statement: For GL_n(F_p), the upper-triangular Borel has index prime to p and the upper-unitriangular subgroup is a p-Sylow. For n=3 its order is p³.
items.note: Use the finite GL/B/U order formula, cancelling the exact p-powers. Ordinary group order does not give a field-dependent lifting assertion by itself.

items.name: Borel negligibility would imply general-linear negligibility
items.statement: Pushout of the B_n reduction extension to coefficients M_n(F_p) is the restriction of the GL_n extension. If the former is negligible then the latter is negligible by prime-to-p index detection.

items.name: Quadratic-unipotent adjoint norm vanishes for p>3
items.statement: For p>3, σ∈GL_n(F_p) of order p with minimal polynomial (t−1)², and X∈M_n(F_p), Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}σ^i Xσ^{-i}=0.
items.note: After Jordan form σ=I+N with N²=0, each entry has degree ≤2 in i. Sums of powers 0,1,2 vanish when p>3. The restriction p>3 is essential.

items.name: Quadratic-unipotent element has no order-p lift for p>3
items.statement: Under Lemma 5.2(1) hypotheses, no lift of σ to GL_n(Z/p²) has order p.
items.note: Choose the square-zero Jordan lift Ñ. (I+Ñ)^p=I+pÑ≠I and multiplying the lift by I+pX changes its pth power by the zero adjoint norm.

items.name: Block projection on the inverse-image group
items.statement: For finite free Z/p²-modules Ṽ,W̃, let E be the inverse image of diag(GL(V),I_W) in GL(Ṽ⊕W̃). The top-left block gives a homomorphism π:E→GL(Ṽ), reducing to GL(V); the kernel-coefficient map is X↦X_VV.
items.note: Correct the draft’s claim that every element preserves Ṽ. Off-diagonal blocks are divisible by p, so their product is zero modulo p²; this, not literal restriction to Ṽ, proves multiplicativity. API: Block extraction, invertibility, reduction square and multiplication formula; maps of the three extension rows. Tests: I+pE_31 for Ṽ spanned by the first two coordinates does not preserve Ṽ, although its top-left block is well-defined. Test the off-diagonal product vanishes modulo p².

items.name: Negligibility descends to a direct summand
items.statement: If the reduction extension for GL(Ṽ⊕W̃) is negligible over F, the reduction extension for GL(Ṽ) is negligible over F.
items.note: Pull back along diag(GL(V),I_W), then push coefficients through the preceding block projection.

items.name: Lifts descend pointwise to a direct summand
items.statement: If diag(ρ,1):Γ_K→GL(V⊕W) has a modulo-p² lift, then its top-left block is a modulo-p² lift of ρ.
items.locator: Lemma 5.3 proof and last paragraph of Theorem 1.4 p.20
items.note: The theorem at the end needs this pointwise strengthening, not just the printed field-universal negligibility implication.

items.name: The Heisenberg group and its subgroups
items.statement: For odd p let U=U₃(F_p), T=(F_p×)³ acting by diagonal conjugation, σ_ij=I+E_ij, N=<σ_12,σ_13>, Z=<σ_13>, S=<σ_23>.
items.note: API: Coordinates (a,b,c), multiplication (a,b,c)(a′,b′,c′)=(a+a′,b+b′,c+c′+ab′), subgroup embeddings and conjugation by T; identify N,Z,S explicitly. Tests: |U|=p³, |N|=p², |Z|=|S|=p; [σ_12,σ_23]=σ_13 in the chosen commutator convention.

items.name: Structure of U₃ at odd primes
items.statement: For odd p, U has exponent p; N is normal, Z is its center and commutator subgroup, U=N⋊S, and T normalizes N,Z,S. Every subgroup of order p² is elementary abelian and contains Z; any such H≠N satisfies NH=U and N∩H=Z. Every order-p subgroup lies in one of order p².
items.note: These elementary group-theoretic statements are explicit prerequisites of Mackey reduction. Split the structural assertions into individual lemmas in the design; do not export exponent p for p=2.

items.name: The restricted reduction class α
items.statement: With A=M₃(F_p) under conjugation, let Ũ be the inverse image of U in GL₃(Z/p²), and α∈H²(U,A) the class of 1→A→Ũ→U→1.
items.note: API: Restriction from GL₃ and B₃; changes of matrix lifts; restriction to N,Z; pullback to an absolute Galois group. Tests: Kernel is all of A, not just the strictly upper-triangular matrices; Ũ is an inverse image, not U₃(Z/p²).

items.name: T-invariance of the reduction class
items.statement: The class α and res_U^N α are T-invariant because α is restricted from the B₃ extension and the inclusions U,N are T-equivariant.
items.note: Use conjugation on both group and coefficients and the compatibility with restriction; inner conjugation acts trivially on the ambient cohomology.

items.name: Nontrivial restriction for p>3
items.statement: For p>3, res_U^Z α≠0, hence res_U^N α≠0.
items.note: An extension splitting over Z would give an order-p lift of σ_13, contradicting Lemma 5.2.

items.name: Modulo-nine norm and commutator identities
items.statement: For A=M₃(F₃), N_σ12(a)=a_21 E_12. The (2,3) entry of −(σ_13−1)a+(σ_12−1)b is a_21. Therefore lifts (I+3a)σ̃_12 and (I+3b)σ̃_13 cannot both have order 3 and commute.
items.note: Order 3 forces a_21=−1 while commutation forces a_21=0. Both linear identities checked on all 3^9 possible a (and the independent b contribution) in exact modular arithmetic.

items.name: Nontrivial restriction including p=3
items.statement: For every odd p, res_U^N α is a nonzero element of H²(N,A)^T.
items.note: At p=3 the restriction to Z itself is zero; the elementary abelian subgroup N is necessary.

items.name: Order-p generators enlarge to order-p² generators
items.statement: If H₁≤H₂≤U and |H_i|=p^i, then Im φ_H₁⊂Im φ_H₂.
items.note: A generator of Hom(H₁,Q/Z) extends across the elementary abelian H₂; the projection formula changes a to N_H₂/H₁(a).

items.name: The central-subgroup generator map ψ_Z
items.statement: Define ψ_Z:A^Z⊗H²(Z,Z)→H²(N,A) by cup product followed by cor_Z^N.
items.note: API: Pure-tensor formula, T-equivariance and relation to res_U^N φ_H when NH=U and N∩H=Z. Tests: The target is H²(N,A), not H²(U,A); reuse corestriction rather than creating a second transfer.

items.name: Mackey reduction of the restricted generated subgroup
items.statement: res_U^N(barH²(U,A)) is contained in the sum of Im(res φ_U), Im(res φ_N), and Im ψ_Z.
items.note: Treat H=1 separately (H²(1,Z)=0), H=U and H=N directly; use the double-coset formula for order-p² H≠N and Claim 5.5 for order p. The proof’s first H²(N,A) should read barH²(U,A).

items.name: Mackey double-coset formula in cohomology
items.statement: For finite H and subgroups P,Q, res_Q^H cor_P^H = Σ_{QgP} cor_{Q∩gPg⁻¹}^Q ∘g_*∘res_{P∩g⁻¹Qg}^P. In particular for normal P, res_P^H cor_P^H is the H/P norm.
items.note: The representation-theoretic Mackey decomposition is built; this cohomology formula is not. Import the upstream planned owner.

items.name: Corestriction transitivity
items.statement: For open finite-index P≤Q≤Γ, cor_P^Γ=cor_Q^Γ∘cor_P^Q in degree two.

items.name: Conjugation commutes with cohomology operations
items.statement: Automorphisms of a group with compatible coefficient action commute with restriction, corestriction, cup products and connecting homomorphisms, on their corresponding subgroup/module maps.
items.note: Reuse the built conjugation and cup carriers; the missing cor/conjugation compatibilities belong to upstream change-of-groups.

items.name: Exactness of T-invariants
items.statement: If finite T has order prime to p, taking T-invariants is exact on F_p[T]-modules, by averaging with |T|⁻¹Σ_t t.
items.note: Use it both to pass to images and to replace generators of an invariant sum by invariant preimages. Do not claim exactness for arbitrary finite groups in characteristic p.

items.name: Diagonal characters and weight lines
items.statement: For t=(t₁,t₂,t₃)∈T, τ_ij(t)=t_i/t_j and F_p(τ_ij) is the one-dimensional representation with that character. T acts on E_ij by τ_ij, whereas it acts on a coordinate character χ_ij of U,N,Z by τ_ji.
items.note: API: Character multiplication/inverse, basis eigenvectors, tensor weights and trivial-character criterion; conjugation on H¹ is χ(t⁻¹ut). Tests: τ_ii=1; at p=3 inverse characters can coincide, so retain the centralizer restriction in the final weight computation.

items.name: Centralizers in the adjoint module
items.statement: For A=M₃(F_p), A^U=<I,E_13>, A^N=<I,E_12,E_13>, and A^Z consists of upper-triangular matrices with entries a_11=a_33 and a_21=a_31=a_32=0.
items.note: The source only needs the upper-triangular containment for A^Z. Prove the exact linear equations by commuting with E_13; p odd in the application.

items.name: Integral cohomology weight spaces
items.statement: Via H²(J,Z)≅Hom(J,Q/Z), H²(U,Z)=F_p(τ_21)⊕F_p(τ_32), H²(N,Z)=F_p(τ_21)⊕F_p(τ_31), and H²(Z,Z)=F_p(τ_31).
items.note: Correct the printed last τ_13 to τ_31, since conjugation on characters is contragredient. Over p=3 these characters happen to agree, but not for general p.

items.name: No invariant generators from U
items.statement: (A^U⊗H²(U,Z))^T=0: its four weights are τ_21,τ_32,τ_23,τ_12, all nontrivial for odd p. Hence Im(res φ_U)^T=0.

items.name: Invariant generators from N
items.statement: (A^N⊗H²(N,Z))^T is spanned by E_12⊗∂χ_12 and E_13⊗∂χ_13, for every odd p including p=3.

items.name: The S-norm kills the second N generator
items.note: Oddness of p is used in the divisibility of p(p−1)/2.

items.name: The first N generator reduces to the U case
items.statement: Since χ_12 extends to U, the projection formula puts φ_N(E_12⊗∂χ_12) in Im φ_U; it is T-invariant, so its restriction to N vanishes by the U-weight computation. Consequently Im(res φ_N)^T=0.
items.note: The draft’s final φ_U(E_12⊗...) has an ill-typed argument: E_12 is not U-invariant. The argument is its relative norm N_U/N(E_12) in A^U.

items.name: Only one invariant centralizer tensor generator
items.statement: (A^Z⊗H²(Z,Z))^T=<E_13⊗∂χ_13>. At p=3 the ambient A tensor has the extra candidate E_31⊗∂χ_13, but E_31∉A^Z.

items.name: Corestriction kills the central generator
items.statement: χ_13 on Z extends to N and E_13∈A^N, so ψ_Z(E_13⊗∂χ_13)=cor_Z^N res_Z^N(E_13∪∂χ_13)=p(E_13∪∂χ_13)=0. Hence Im ψ_Z has zero T-invariants.

items.name: Vanishing of T-invariants in the restricted generated subgroup
items.statement: For odd p, (res_U^N(barH²(U,A)))^T=0.
items.note: This is invariants of the image. Averaging and T-equivariance justify passage from the three generator spaces to their images.

items.name: Non-negligibility of the U-extension with enough roots
items.statement: For odd p and F containing μ_p², α∉barH²(U,A)=H²_neg,F(U,A).
items.note: Its restriction is a nonzero T-invariant class by Claim 5.4, whereas every invariant class in the image of the generated subgroup is zero by Claim 5.7.

items.name: General-linear reduction extension is not negligible
items.statement: For every odd prime p, every n≥3 and every field F of characteristic different from p, the GL_n reduction extension is not negligible over F.
items.note: Extend F to contain μ_p² using base-extension monotonicity, use n=3 U obstruction and descend negligibility contrapositively through the pointwise block map.

items.name: Borel reduction extension is not negligible
items.statement: For every odd prime p, every n≥3 and every field F of characteristic different from p, the B_n reduction extension is not negligible over F.
items.note: Follows from Borel→GL implication and the preceding theorem. There is no roots-of-unity hypothesis in this final non-negligibility statement.

items.name: A simpler central test when p>3
items.statement: For p>3, res_U^Z α≠0 but res_U^Z(barH²(U,A))=0, so the center already detects non-negligibility.
items.note: Derive the second assertion using the zero norm on A and the double-coset formula; expand this alternative proof in the design rather than referring to an unspecified computation.

items.name: The central restriction splits when p=3
items.statement: For p=3, res_U^Z α=0: σ_13 has an order-three lift, for example (I−3E_31)(I+E_13) in GL₃(Z/9).
items.note: The displayed witness was checked by exact matrix multiplication. This does not split the N-extension.

items.name: The nonzero N-restriction is negligible
items.statement: For odd p, μ_p²⊂F, N=<I+E_12,I+E_13> and A=M₃(F_p), res_U^N α=E_12 cup δχ_12+E_13 cup δχ_13 in H²(N,A). Hence it lies in barH²(N,A)=H²_neg,F(N,A), although Claim 5.4 proves it is nonzero.
items.note: RESOLVED in continuation codex-a71f92: least-residue matrix sections have factor set κ(a,c)E_12+κ(b,d)E_13, where κ(x,y)=floor((x+y)/p); δ of a/p mod Z is κ. Both E-directions are N-invariant. Use the cup map for ambient N, not φ_N with target H²(U,A). Independently, lift both characters by Kummer and combine their square-zero directions. See /126–/133 and the report. This proof is supplied here, not printed in the source.

items.name: Faithful p-dimensional Heisenberg representation
items.statement: For odd p and F containing a primitive pth root ζ, construct a faithful representation U₃(F_p)→GL_p(F) using a cyclic shift and diagonal matrices diag(1,ζ,…,ζ^{p−1}), with the center acting by ζ or its explicitly fixed inverse.
items.note: API: Fix the shift direction so the commutator equals the chosen central generator; normal form in U, matrix action, faithfulness and dimension. Tests: Both generators have order p, their commutator is nontrivial scalar; p=3 matrices; μ_p⊂F and char F≠p are required.

items.name: Chu–Kang rational invariant field input
items.statement: Let p be prime, G a p-group of order at most p⁴, e(G)=p^r, and char F≠p with μ_p^r⊂F. For every finite-dimensional linear G-representation V/F, F(V)^G is purely transcendental over F. In particular for the faithful p-dimensional U₃ representation at odd p, F(V)^U≅F(x₁,…,x_p).
items.locator: Theorem 1.4 proof p.19, citing CK01 Theorem 1.6; CK01 publisher abstract
items.note: Primary publisher abstract directly read and matches the hypotheses quoted in the main proof; CK01 full proof was not accessible. A design job must read that paper and supply its rationality proof, not replace rationality by stable rationality. The number of variables follows since the finite fixed-field extension preserves transcendence degree.

items.name: The explicit generic residual representation
items.statement: Take the above V, K=F(V)^U and L=F(V), embed L in K^sep, then compose Γ_K→U with U⊂GL₃(F_p) to obtain ρ. Transport K along its F-isomorphism with F(x₁,…,x_p).
items.note: API: Surjective quotient Γ_K→U, faithful inclusion, continuity, coefficient action and transport along field isomorphisms. Tests: The matrix image is U; the field has p algebraically independent variables, not a bound depending on n.

items.name: The generic three-dimensional representation does not lift
items.statement: The preceding ρ over K=F(x₁,…,x_p) has no continuous lift to GL₃(Z/p²).
items.note: A lift would lift Γ_K→U through Ũ. Generic vanishing would make α negligible, contradicting Theorem 5.1. Only μ_p⊂F is required for constructing K; μ_p² was used after a field extension in the non-negligibility proof.

items.name: Nonliftable representations in every dimension at least three
items.statement: For every odd p, every field F containing a primitive pth root and every n≥3, there exists continuous Γ_{F(x₁,…,x_p)}→GL_n(F_p) with no continuous modulo-p² lift. Take diag(ρ,I_{n−3}).
items.note: Use the pointwise block-projection lemma so the obstruction persists over the same field; the universal negligibility statement alone is insufficient for this last sentence.

items.name: Negative answer even with all roots of unity
items.statement: For odd p and n≥3, choosing F containing all roots of unity still yields a nonliftable GL_n representation; the same upper-triangular residual representation cannot have a B_n lift. Thus Question 1.1 and Conjecture 1.2 are false.
items.note: The residual ρ has image in U₃ and its padded image is upper triangular, so the specific witness also defeats the flag-lifting conjecture. Do not infer that every residual representation fails to lift.

items.name: Characteristic-p boundary
items.statement: If char K=p, then H²(Γ_K,M)=0 for every finite p-primary discrete Γ_K-module M. Consequently the GL_n and B_n reduction extensions are negligible over any base field of characteristic p.
items.note: This uses cd_p(Γ_K)≤1 (Artin–Schreier and dévissage), not the rational-variable nonlifting argument. Upstream ProfiniteCohomology Layer 11 defines dimension but does not explicitly include this field theorem; supply the field-specific proof here.

items.name: Finite-group cohomology commutes with direct sums of trivial coefficients
items.statement: For finite H and a free abelian group P, H^i(H,P)≅H^i(H,Z)⊗P, naturally in P; finite bar cochains give the direct-sum comparison.
items.note: Needed for both ends of the length-one free resolution argument; do not assume finite generation of P.

items.name: Finite coefficient cohomology is annihilated by its exponent
items.statement: If nA=0 as an H-module, then nH^i(H,A)=0 for all i≥0, by the same assertion on the cochain complex. In particular H²(N,M₃(F_p)) is p-torsion.

items.name: Generic base change of invariant fields
items.statement: For a finite faithful linear H-action on V/F and a field extension F′/F, the base-changed action remains faithful, and the generic H-torsor is the base change of F(V)/F(V)^H on suitable nonempty opens; this supplies naturality of γ and its constant restriction.
items.note: Use generic torsors and the induced embeddings after choosing the relevant function fields. Do not identify F′⊗_F F(V) with the full rational function field without localization.

items.name: Integral cyclic carry cocycle
items.statement: For m≥1 and a,c∈C_m represented in {0,…,m−1}, κ_m(a,c)=floor((a+c)/m)∈Z. It is normalized and satisfies κ(a,c)+κ(a+c mod m,e)=κ(c,e)+κ(a,c+e mod m).
items.note: API: Least residues, carry, normalization and integral cocycle identity; coefficient reduction modulo n. Tests: m=1 gives zero; κ_m(m−1,1)=1 for m>1; retain integral values until reduction. Proof: both sides equal floor((a+c+e)/m).

items.name: Carry represents the integral character boundary
items.statement: For χ:C_m→Q/Z, χ(a)=a/m mod Z, the connecting class δχ for 0→Z→Q→Q/Z→0 is represented by κ_m. Pushing coefficients Z→Z/n gives the class of 0→Z/n→Z/mn→C_m→0, with kernel inclusion multiplication by m.
items.locator: Example 2.2; Remark 4.3; derived formula for Remark 5.8(2)
items.note: Lift χ by q(a)=a/m∈Q and use dq(a,c)=q(c)−q(a+c)+q(a). The section a↦a∈Z/mn has defect mκ_m. Test m=n=p and the positive carry at (p−1,1); do not confuse this connecting map with negative Hochschild–Serre transgression.

items.name: Compatible Kummer characters lift through cyclic reduction
items.statement: Let m,n≥1, K contain a primitive mn-th root ζ_mn, and ζ_m=ζ_mn^n. Under these compatible constant-cyclic identifications, H¹(K,Z/mn)→H¹(K,Z/m) is K×/(K×)^mn→K×/(K×)^m and is surjective. Every continuous Γ_K→Z/m therefore lifts continuously to Z/mn.
items.locator: Example 2.2, expanded naturality proof for Remark 5.8(2)
items.note: For u∈K× choose γ^(mn)=u and β=γ^n. The character gγ/γ maps to gβ/β under nth power. Cohomology equality is equality of characters since constant coefficients have zero degree-one coboundaries. Continuity follows from finite separable root extensions. Import upstream full Kummer /18, not merely the pinned injective class map /19. Keep the primitive mn-root hypothesis; no claim of necessity.

items.name: Least-residue section of the row-unipotent subgroup
items.statement: For N≅F_p² embedded as I+aE_12+bE_13, set s(a,b)=I+āE_12+b̄E_13∈GL₃(Z/p²) with least residues. Its inverse is I−āE_12−b̄E_13 and its reduction is (a,b).
items.note: API: Section, inverse, reduction and normalization at zero. Tests: All products E_1i E_1j vanish for i,j∈{2,3}; s is not a homomorphism; the pair (p−1,0),(1,0) has defect pE_12.

items.name: Row-unipotent section defect is the pair of carries
items.statement: For x=(a,b),y=(c,d)∈N, s(x)s(y)s(x+y)^−1=I+p(κ_p(a,c)E_12+κ_p(b,d)E_13). Under X↦I+pX this is a representative of res_U^N α.
items.note: Multiply using the square-zero row directions. The kernel remains the full adjoint A although the representative lands in a two-dimensional N-fixed subspace. Test both coordinates and p=3,5,7,11; the identity also works at p=2 without implying a headline nonlifting theorem.

items.name: N-class cup decomposition has ambient group N
items.statement: For χ_12(a,b)=a/p mod Z and χ_13(a,b)=b/p mod Z, res_U^N α=E_12 cup δχ_12+E_13 cup δχ_13. These are generators for N≤N, so the class belongs to barH²(N,A) without any corestriction to U.
items.locator: Remark 5.8(2), derived from the preceding carry formulas
items.note: N fixes both coefficient directions; the (0,2) cup is coefficient multiplication of the scalar carry, giving equality of representatives. Apply Theorem 1.3 with H=N and both exponents p. Test that no cor_N^U occurs: res_U^N cor_N^U is an S-norm, the different map used in Claim 5.7.

items.name: Continuous weak matrix lift for every N-valued representation
items.statement: For μ_p²⊂K and continuous ρ=(χ₁,χ₂):Γ_K→N, choose Kummer lifts χ̃_i:Γ_K→Z/p² and put ρ̃(g)=I+χ̃₁(g)E_12+χ̃₂(g)E_13. This is a continuous homomorphism into B₃(Z/p²) reducing to ρ.
items.locator: Remark 5.8(2), independent weak-lifting proof supplied in continuation
items.note: API: Constructor from character lifts; evaluation, multiplicativity, continuity and reduction; restriction in K for fixed choices. No canonical choice or uniqueness is asserted. Tests: Zero, one and two nonzero characters; no surjectivity requirement. Square-zero directions make multiplication additive and determinant one. Uses only /128 and obstruction /8, not classification /70.

items.name: Restriction of negligible subgroups need not be surjective
items.statement: For odd p and μ_p²⊂F in §5, restriction H²_neg,F(U,A)→H²_neg,F(N,A) is not surjective: res_U^N α is negligible but nonzero and T-invariant, whereas the T-invariants in res_U^N(barH²(U,A)) vanish.
items.locator: Remark 5.8(2), Claims 5.4/5.7 and Theorem 1.3; derived corollary
items.note: Use invariants of the image, not just images of invariant elements: even a non-invariant preimage cannot map to this nonzero invariant target. This reconciles the ambient-N cup formula with the U-obstruction. No claim is made for arbitrary p=2 or inadequate roots.
